accepted_claims.claim: For normalized Haar measure in the ordinary operator-norm radius-X ball of SL3(R), the probability log(sigma1/sigma2)>=s tends to 2 exp(-2s)-exp(-4s).
accepted_claims.scope: Every fixed s>=0; ordinary positive singular values; continuous Haar measure.

accepted_claims.claim: Under the intended limit-of-normalized-volumes interpretation, the eta^(-4) numerical upper bound of Fuchs-Rivin Theorem 3.4 fails in dimension three.
accepted_claims.scope: The theorem explicitly uses positive KAK diagonal entries and eta>4. At threshold eta^2 the actual limit is 2eta^(-4)-eta^(-8). Literal separately divergent limits are not assigned a quotient.

accepted_claims.claim: The first audit formula (A) for I(L,s) is correct for 0<=s<=3L/2, with zero mass for s>=3L/2.
accepted_claims.scope: L=log X>0; radial normalization as specified in derivations.md.

accepted_claims.claim: The first audit formula K(L)=sinh(4L)/16-sinh(3L)/6+sinh(2L)/16+L/8 is correct.
The inverse-bounded-to-ordinary Haar-volume ratio is asymptotic to 6X^(-2).
accepted_claims.scope: Continuous SL3(R), ordinary operator-radius X; no claim for SL3(Z).

documentary_clarification: The source has nearby square-eigenvalue terminology inconsistent with its explicit KAK decomposition. The latter fixes the ordinary singular-value convention; neither alternate squared-value nor squared-radius readings rescue the numerical bound.
